title: The women who asked for a day
hook: women asked the Prophet ﷺ for a day to teach them, and he gave it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Uways, the man of Yemen whose prayer Umar sought. Your line was he stayed with his mother.

A complaint, made out loud, to the Prophet himself. The men, a group of women tell him, have taken all of your time. Every gathering, every lesson, the men are there first, crowding in. So the women make a request: set aside a day for us, just for us, when we can come and learn from you. It's a few lines in Sahih al-Bukhari, the kind of request that could be brushed off with a vague promise. Today: the women who asked for a day.
screen: `THE MEN HAVE TAKEN YOUR TIME.` → `SET ASIDE A DAY FOR US.` → `WHAT WILL HE SAY?`

segments.voice: Bukhari places this report in his book on knowledge, narrated by the companion Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. The women come to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and name the problem plainly. They don't ask for a favor. They ask for a day. And the hadith says he promised them one, and kept it: he met them on that day, and he advised them and taught them. So teaching was not something that happened to women by accident, overheard from the back of a room. When they asked, a time was made for them on purpose, and the Prophet showed up. Then a glimpse of what was said. He told them that a woman who loses three of her children will find them a shield for her from the Fire. And one woman, in the middle of the lesson, asks: and two? He says: and two. These women brought their real lives into the room, including the grief of losing a child, and the teaching met them there. And a woman felt free to interrupt and ask about her own case. That is a day for learning: a set time, a teacher who arrives, and room for the question you actually have. In the same book on knowledge, Aisha is remembered praising the women of the Ansar, because shyness did not stop them from learning their religion. The request for a day sits in that company.
screen: `THEY NAMED THE PROBLEM.` · `HE PROMISED A DAY, AND KEPT IT.` · `THEY BROUGHT THEIR REAL GRIEF.` · `ROOM FOR THE NEXT QUESTION.` · then, large: `A DAY FOR LEARNING.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who has asked you, maybe more than once, to show them something: how to cook a dish, read a page of Arabic, fix a bike, pray a prayer. Maybe you said, sure, sometime. Picture their face, and give that sometime a real day and an hour, with room for their question.
Ansar. The helpers of Medina, whose women asked the Prophet for a day of their own, and he gave it and taught them. Today's word.
Your line: a day for learning. They asked, and a time was made on purpose. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims cite this report from Sahih al-Bukhari when talking about women's study of the religion, and mosques and communities hold classes and circles for women.

options: They asked for their own day, and he set one and taught them.
They mostly learned secondhand, from what their husbands repeated.

chat.meaning: In Bukhari, the women said the men had taken his time; he promised them a day, kept it, and taught them.

Ansar.meaning: the helpers: the Muslims of Medina

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.meaning: the companion who narrated this report

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings

Aisha.meaning: the Prophet's wife, who praised the Ansar women
